description: gate.py's paper-pass producer can never observe a single resolved trade, so PM_PAPER_PASS is mathematically stuck at 0 forever regardless of how many paper trades decide.py records or how profitable the underlying momentum strategy actually is. gate.py's `_load_resolved()` (gate.py:44) only counts a ledger row toward the gate if `r.get("status") == "resolved" and "pnl_usdc" in r`. But decide.py -- the ONLY writer to this ledger that run.sh actually invokes (run.sh:21) -- writes rows with `"status": "open"` and NEVER writes `"status": "resolved"` or a `"pnl_usdc"` key anywhere (decide.py:91-93); there is no resolution/settlement step anywhere in decide.py, gate.py, or run.sh that would ever transition an open paper row to resolved. The only script in this codebase that ever sets `status = "resolved"` is pm-paper.py's resolve() function (pm-paper.py:132), but that function is (a) never called by run.sh -- it is a separate, unwired CLI action -- and (b) uses an entirely different field name, `"realized_pnl"`, not `"pnl_usdc"` (pm-paper.py:132: `r["realized_pnl"] = round(pnl, 4)`), and requires fields (`shares_held`, `outcome_index`) that decide.py's row schema does not contain at all. Concretely: if pm-paper.py resolve() were ever run against the shared ledger file (both scripts point at the identical path `~/loops/earn-pm-trade/paper-positions.jsonl`), it would raise `KeyError: 'shares_held'` on the very first row decide.py ever wrote (pm-paper.py:130: `payout = r["shares_held"] * 1.0 if won else 0.0`). This is fail-CLOSED (money-safe -- the gate can never spuriously pass), but it means REQ-PMTRADE(b)'s mandate to 'clear the paper-mode gate before any real stake' can literally never be satisfied by the current pipeline as wired -- not a strategy-quality problem, a missing-code problem: nothing in the shipped slot ever produces a schema-compatible resolved+pnl_usdc row for decide.py's own paper trades.
